primary_references.use: Confirms Internal TargetUri is a relative reference interpreted against its source part/package; external resource URI is not interchangeable with a ZIP filename.
Internal reference may be a package absolute path beginning / or a relative path. It cannot be an absolute URI with a scheme.

Reference grammar distinguishes authority, path-absolute and path-noscheme; colon in the first relative path segment is not a path-noscheme. Query/fragment are separate URI components, not filename suffixes.
GetZipItemNameFromOpcName strips the leading /; escaped text is not unquoted into path separators by that mapping. Used as an implementation comparison, not universal package compatibility proof.

limitations: Shared URI resolver intentionally supports whole-part references; query/fragment targets are rejected/unsupported, not universally declared invalid for every format-defined relationship.

Percent escapes are preserved exactly; full percent-hex/Unicode/case equivalence, Content_Types semantics and all OPC/IRI/schema validation remain unverified. Full unreserved-alias equivalence is not implemented.
Valid relative/absolute roots, DOCX/PPTX conventional target paths and selected escaped paths are covered by pure resolver tables; no new full native DOCX/PPTX/model pipelines claimed.
Preflight adds one worksheet parse pass before projection without holding all trees; no large-file performance/resource certification.
Empty-sink contract covers the tested binding and direct sheetData defects, not arbitrary later cell/style/media exceptions. process_file remains the persisted shard rollback boundary.
Unchanged existing native openpyxl route, cell payload/shared strings/style/defined-name parsing and general XLSX feature gaps remain outside scope.
No safe SQLite/answer, full Layer1 class setup, build package, GUI, original personal source or model acceptance run. No commit/push/release.
